clue.text: Many letters received after a number of animals shot

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
a bag is the tally of game shot on a hunt

explanation.surface: A tally of game birds brought down by guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a placement instruction, but it is a Latin translation, as in postwar or postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the mail a person or office gets, especially a large quantity of correspondence.

clue.text: That's one in the eye for scholar

definitions.meaning: the dark opening in the centre of the eye

explanation.surface: A schoolchild receives an insult, 'one in the eye' being a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupil names both the dark round aperture of the eye and a learner at school.

clue.text: Presenter and what her voice may come from

definitions.meaning: a ... gives a talk or presentation

definitions.text: what her voice may come from
definitions.meaning: a loudspeaker is what carries her voice to the audience

explanation.surface: A woman giving a talk, with her voice relayed through equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaker is both a person who addresses an audience and a loudspeaker device.

clue.text: Many Britons so classified graduate with me

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate tells you that, like them, many Britons fall into this category.
explanation.definitionFit: BAME, Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic, is a UK classification covering many British people.

clue.text: Carried away by current film?

definitions.meaning: something swept off by a moving stream of air is ...

explanation.surface: Something swept off in a flow, perhaps of electricity, or a cinema classic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes anything blown away for good, and is also the title of the famous Civil War film.

clue.text: Scowling, dropping some flour in gravy

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are kept, the rest are dropped, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A cook frowns while sprinkling a little flour into the gravy to thicken it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the second letter of 'flour' through to the G of 'gravy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour (or lower) is to frown or look sullen, so louring is a scowling look.

clue.text: Is it unfair to ask these of the wealthy?

definitions.text: Is it unfair to ask these of the wealthy?

parts.words: Is it unfair to ask these of the wealthy?
parts.note: loaded means both biased (of a query) and rich, so these queries could be put to people with money

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it is fair to quiz rich people.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaded question contains an unfair assumption; 'loaded' is also slang for very rich.

clue.text: Not in position to admit girl that's too good to ignore

indicators.note: to let in, so the girl goes inside the other word

parts.note: unable means not in a position to do something
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone cannot let in a young woman who is irresistible.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmissable describes something so good you must not miss it, like a show.

clue.text: Embed Mike into one factory

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the combined word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a plant is a factory
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Placing a man named Mike inside a single works, perhaps as a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to fix something firmly in, to embed it.

clue.text: Tackle receiving poor pay in intermediate period

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other

parts.note: tackle is equipment, gear

indicators.note: badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kit bought on low wages for a stopgap stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts the anagram made by 'poor' inside the synonym for tackle, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is a year off between school and university, an in-between stretch.

clue.text: Illness being new, complaining more to listeners

indicators.note: the words are to be heard rather than read, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: new plus moanier, more given to complaining, said together

explanation.surface: A sick person whose fresh ailment makes them grumble even more to those around them.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW-MOANIER said quickly sounds like the disease; the P is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is an infection inflaming the lungs, a serious respiratory disease.

clue.text: Finish cleaning second little pet

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second ('half a mo')
a pup is a young dog, a small pet

explanation.surface: A quick moment spent with a small pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to complete a cleaning job by wiping away the last of the spillage.

clue.text: Boy, by complete coincidence, not female

indicators.note: the abbreviation for female, the letter F, is to be left out

parts.note: a fluke is a pure stroke of chance

explanation.surface: A lad met entirely by chance, and not a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is a boy's name, standing for any male child in crosswords.

clue.text: Domestic cleaner's opinion of lottery

parts.note: a chimney sweep cleans in the home; with the possessive this gives sweep's
a take is a view or opinion, as in 'my take on it'

explanation.surface: What the chimney sweep thinks about the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a gamble in which all the stakes are pooled and won by drawing lots, a kind of raffle.

clue.text: Thus raised concern about untrained playwright

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: around, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: care is concern
wild means untamed, untrained

explanation.surface: Worry about an untaught dramatist has been brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suits a down entry, read upwards; 'about' wraps the concern round the untrained piece, splitting it before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish author of The Importance of Being Earnest, a famous dramatist.

clue.text: Sport I play in good health

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them around freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking part in sport keeps you in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good health' looks like a state, but it is the toast said when drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast meaning 'may it benefit you', the same as 'cheers'.

clue.text: Dismember hanged traitor? Mercy!

definitions.meaning: to cut a hanged traitor's body into four parts
... is clemency shown to a defeated foe, as in 'give no ...'

explanation.surface: A condemned traitor's grisly end, with a cry for pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging, drawing and quartering was the old English punishment for treason; separately, quarter means sparing an enemy's life.

clue.text: No relaxation, enclosing a direction for poetry

indicators.note: one piece wraps round another, so the next word's letters go inside

parts.note: rest is relaxation

explanation.surface: A tireless poet keeps heading off in a new direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor'east is a poetic or nautical contraction of northeast, a compass point.

clue.text: Number fed on bananas, very many

indicators.note: crazy, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Many have been fed on bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: No end of means a huge amount, countless.

clue.text: Old soldier, a camp entertainer

definitions.meaning: ... were British soldiers of past centuries, named for their red tunics
an entertainer at a Butlin's holiday camp

explanation.surface: A veteran now amusing guests at a holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat names both an 18th-century British soldier and staff at Butlin's, a British chain of holiday camps.

clue.text: Recruit is strangely silent

indicators.note: the letters behave oddly, i.e. form a new order

explanation.surface: A new soldier who oddly says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone, or to join up yourself, is to enlist in the armed forces.

clue.text: Perhaps seen from Torquay hotel window, ie waves crashing

definitions.text: Perhaps seen from Torquay hotel window

indicators.note: falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest at a seaside hotel watches breakers hit the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea view is an outlook over the ocean, an example being from a coastal hotel room.

clue.text: Settlements in town send me nuts

indicators.note: crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the housing estates in their town are driving them mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowments are funds or property settled on an institution or person, legal settlements of money.

clue.text: Pointed criticism of second pub?

parts.note: a bar is a pub
B is the second letter, as in B-grade or plan B

explanation.surface: A remark about a second-rate inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting, hurtful remark, likened to the sharp backward point of a hook.

clue.text: Needed as substitutes? Come off it!

definitions.text: Needed as substitutes? Come off it!

parts.words: Needed as substitutes? Come off it!
parts.note: reserve players wait on a seat beside the pitch and come off it when sent on

explanation.surface: A scornful retort to the claim that some reserves are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench is where substitutes sit in team sports; 'on the bench' means being a reserve.

clue.text: Pretty fine appearance

definitions.meaning: ... appearance, being pleasant to look at, is a meaning of ...

explanation.surface: Someone looks rather good.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair has senses of beautiful, of dry sunny weather, and of a comely look.

clue.text: As slaver, master holding nothing back

indicators.note: the built word is read from the end backwards
one word holds the other within it

parts.note: a lord is a master
O, the round zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A slave-owner keeps everything for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slaver' looks like a slave trader, but it is the verb to dribble. 'holding' puts O inside LORD; 'back' turns LOORD around.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, which is to dribble.

clue.text: Is old cat welcoming a time in quarantine?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the big cat takes in the following letters as a host takes in guests

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Is the elderly cat letting someone in while kept apart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts A and T inside LION, after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a period of enforced separation to stop disease spreading, i.e. being kept apart.

clue.text: Idiot parent ignoring last notice

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is disregarded and dropped

parts.note: a father is a parent
an ad, an advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A foolish parent pays no heed to the latest warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, a blockhead.

clue.text: By the way, threw out mild oath

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: out of order or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone casually remarks that a person let slip a gentle curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a phrase meaning incidentally, but 'By' only joins ST to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is a dated exclamation of surprise, a softened form of 'God's truth'.
